newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices ease before weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices ease before weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices eased slightly Friday ahead of the weekend, pressured by expectations that mild weather over the much of the nation would continue to limit demand, industry sources said.
Despite the steady pace of storage injections, traders said cooling loads were non-existent in most regions and expected to stay that way through next week.

"Most people thought we'd be up today but cash stalled early. There's rain in Texas and some cooler weather coming in," said a trader, noting U.S. Gulf Coast swing prices eased a couple of cents today to the mid-to-high $1.80s/mmBtu.
In the Midcontinent, prices were a few cents lower in the low-to-mid $1.70s, more than five cents over September indices.
Gas in west Texas on El Paso Permian was down slightly to the mid-$1.60s, still over index. South Texas gas lost a few cents to about the $1.80 level, about five cents over Sept 1 levels.
New York city gate weekend gas was talked in the $2.05-2.10 area, down about five cents on the day.
While favorable cash-to-futures spreads were likely to keep injections high this month, traders said builds were likely to slow next month and back more supply into the market as caverns fill.
